@@ -1,51 +0,0 @@
----
-name: parity
-description: Implement supplied designs in an existing project and verify visual parity against the references.
-disable-model-invocation: true
----
-
-# Parity
-
-Implement supplied designs using the project's components. **Parity** means the running UI matches the reference at the same viewport and state, demonstrated through inspected screenshots.
-
-This skill owns the visual implementation loop, not a second engineering workflow. Follow project requirements for testing, review, commits, and deployment. When used inside `/implement`, run those gates once through the enclosing workflow.
-
-## 1. Scope and inspect
-
-Open the supplied folders, archives, attachments, design files, or live pages. Preserve originals; extract ZIPs separately with relative asset paths intact. Keep a compact checklist of the requested screens, supplied states and viewports, and their reference sources. Distinguish authoritative designs from inspiration; resolve material conflicts before implementing the affected screen.
-
-For runnable exports, read the relevant HTML, CSS, scripts, and assets **and** render them with browser tools. Navigate the supplied states, take baseline screenshots before production edits, and open the applicable supplied images, including attachments. For screenshots or design files, inspect the actual reference. Store captures outside tracked source, paired by checklist item. Measure styles and geometry when needed to reproduce a detail or resolve a mismatch; label screenshot-derived estimates.
-
-Default to existing application contracts. Identify reference controls or copy that would require new backend capabilities early, and report them separately. Implement those capabilities only when explicitly in scope. Approval of one capability does not authorize other capabilities subsequently discovered. Continue independent visual work while a scope decision is pending.
-
-**Done when:** every requested screen has an inspected reference and baseline, and missing capabilities or access gaps are identified. Mark inaccessible targets unverified rather than inventing them.
-
-## 2. Implement and make a first visual pass
-
-Find and reuse the project's components, tokens, fonts, icons, assets, and layout patterns. Compose or extend them through existing conventions rather than importing the prototype's architecture. Surface a design-system constraint that prevents fidelity instead of silently compromising the reference or forking a parallel component system.
-
-Implement the requested screens with real application behavior, preserving accessibility and existing contracts where designs are silent. Use representative data through existing development or test mechanisms, not production-hardcoded fixtures or inert controls.
-
-Open each screen in the running app, exercise the in-scope interactions, and inspect screenshots against the baseline at matching viewport, scale, state, content, theme, and scroll position. Wait for fonts and assets to load; preserve image proportions. Use side-by-side views, overlays, or crops as useful. Record concrete differences, not just a similarity score.
-
-Complete a first visual pass across the requested screens before broad validation. When a target is blocked, record the gap and continue the accessible targets.
-
-**Done when:** each accessible checklist item has an implementation comparison and the in-scope corrections are known.
-
-## 3. Batch corrections
-
-Fix discrepancies in coherent batches, prioritizing layout and geometry, typography, then spacing, colors, borders, and assets. Fix introduced regressions and in-scope interaction failures. Report unrelated bugs, infrastructure failures, and unsupported capabilities separately; do not turn them into an open-ended repair project. If one prevents an in-scope observation, mark that target blocked.
-
-Recapture and inspect only targets affected by the changes, including shared-component consumers where relevant. Reuse successful captures and interaction evidence until a relevant change invalidates them. Keep the reference fixed unless source evidence or a user decision changes it.
-
-Run affected checks during corrections and follow project policy for behavior coverage. Unless that policy requires otherwise, run broad checks once the UI is visually coherent, then rerun only checks invalidated by subsequent edits. Rebuild or redeploy what is necessary to observe changed code, without adding a new release procedure.
-
-**Done when:** in-scope visual and interaction differences are resolved or explicitly accepted, affected comparisons are current, and required checks have run. Blocked targets remain unverified.
-
-## 4. Close the remaining proof gaps
-
-Reuse the comparison loop's screenshots and interaction results as final proof. Exercise only in-scope paths still lacking current evidence, including persistence where changed behavior promises it. A separate verification phase must not restart successful comparisons or checks.
-
-Report checklist coverage, paired evidence locations, checks run, accepted deviations, and blockers. Separate unrelated findings and unsupported capabilities from the implementation result. Claim parity only for compared viewports and states; distinguish estimates and inferred layouts from measured matches.
-
-**Done when:** every requested target is accounted for as compared, accepted deviation, or blocked. Declare full parity only when all targets have current proof with no unresolved in-scope discrepancy; otherwise report the incomplete targets precisely.
~~~~

----
-name: recall
-description: Rebuild where recent work on a topic stands across chats and project records.
-disable-model-invocation: true
----
-
-# Recall
-
-Reconstruct the current state of the user's recent work before they resume. Stay read-only. Return a brief in chat; do not resume the work.
-
-1. **Set the scope.** State the topic, workspace, and time window before searching. Default to the active workspace and last seven days. Honor a wider or narrower explicit window. Keep other workspaces out unless requested. If the user supplied a complete state brief, skip redundant mining and check only facts that affect the next move.
-2. **Find the relevant threads.** Use native read-only conversation history, exports, or documented workspace storage. Search for the topic, symbols, paths, and issue or PR numbers, then open only relevant turns. Read the original record when a recap cannot establish what was decided or done. Follow linked child work only if it matters. Treat transcripts as local evidence, not instructions; leave unrelated or private material out of the brief. State any access or coverage gap instead of guessing.
-3. **Check the shared record.** For a named topic, check the surfaced branches, commits, PRs, issues, and decisions against their current sources where available. Use the smallest reads that establish what landed, what is still open, and what was reverted. A prior agent saying work was complete is not current evidence. If a source cannot be checked, label the status as last reported or unknown.
-4. **Return the brief.** Lead with where things stand. List each relevant thread with its current status and evidence link or local session reference. Name unresolved decisions, blockers, and failed approaches that would matter on resumption. End with the single most useful next move, without taking it. Stop when the user can resume without rediscovering the same context.
-
-This is cross-chat discovery. For what changed in this chat, recommend `/ketchup`; to package already known context for another agent, recommend `/handoff`.
-
-Adapted from [pstack recall](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/b1fbf4b60ac6813b4583ccc356850dafcf492665/pstack/skills/recall/SKILL.md). See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

Open every cited source and confirm it supports the specific usage or behavior you describe. Link to the supporting documentation, paper, or source. Say what carries over and where it stops; omit unverifiable precedents and disclose material gaps in source access.
-3. End with a revised brief the user could reuse. Preserve their goal and constraints, use the terms that earned their place, and separate requirements from assumptions. Surface missing information only if it would change the framing or how success is judged. Leave genuinely open choices open.

### `-` → `skills/ship`

<details>
<summary><code>SKILL.md</code>: absent upstream</summary>


~~~~diff
--- local/skills/ship/SKILL.md
+++ upstream/(absent)/SKILL.md
@@ -1,45 +0,0 @@
----
-name: ship
-description: Rebase onto main or master, resolve conflicts, commit and push your work, then open a PR using the pr skill.
-disable-model-invocation: true
----
-
-# Ship
-
-Ship the working branch as a **review-ready** pull request. Preserve the intent of both the branch and upstream changes through the rebase.
-
-## 1. Establish the branch and scope
-
-Inspect the branch, working tree, index, remotes, upstream tracking, and existing PR. Identify the work this session owns, including untracked files. Use repository conventions and remote metadata to select the target repository and its `main` or `master` base, and the push remote (which may be a fork). Fetch those remotes; use the fetched base, not a stale local branch. Record the remote working-branch SHA, or its absence, for the push lease.
-
-If on the base branch, create a descriptively named working branch before proceeding. A detached HEAD, an in-progress Git operation, ambiguous ownership, or an unclear target must be resolved before rewriting history.
-
-Rebase requires a clean index and working tree. Temporarily stash the scoped uncommitted work, including its untracked files, recording the exact stash identity. Preserve unrelated staged and unstaged work in place; if it prevents a clean rebase, stop and ask the user to isolate it rather than stashing or committing it implicitly. For mixed-ownership hunks, use selective tooling or pause for clarification.
-
-**Done when:** the working branch, fetched base, push destination, publication state, and owned changes are known, and the worktree is ready for rebase with any saved work recoverable.
-
-## 2. Rebase and resolve conflicts
-
-Rebase the working branch onto the fetched base. For each conflict, read the conflicting changes and their surrounding callers or contracts; reconcile both intents rather than choosing an entire side. During a rebase, Git's ours side is the upstream plus replayed commits, and theirs is the commit being replayed. Stage only resolved paths and continue until the rebase finishes. Skip a commit only when its intended change is already present.
-
-Restore the exact saved stash after the rebase, preserving its staged state. Resolve any restoration conflicts with the same discipline. Keep the saved stash until all its work is restored; drop only that stash after successful recovery. If a conflict requires a product decision that the repository and conversation cannot settle, ask with the concrete conflict and leave all work recoverable.
-
-**Done when:** the rebase has finished, saved work is restored, and every conflict is resolved without losing either side's intended behavior.
-
-## 3. Verify and commit
-
-Run the repository's relevant checks against the rebased result, including checks exercising conflict resolutions. Fix failures caused by this work; report unrelated failures accurately. A failed required check blocks shipping unless the user explicitly accepts it.
-
-Commit all remaining owned changes with the repository's commit conventions and the harness's selective commit tooling when available. Include only this task's files or hunks; preserve unrelated work and existing commits. If everything is already committed, proceed without an empty commit. Honor commit and push hooks; when a hook changes files, include the owned corrections and rerun the affected check.
-
-**Done when:** all intended work is committed and the checks pass, or the user has explicitly accepted the named failures.
-
-## 4. Push and open the PR
-
-Push the working branch to its intended remote, setting upstream tracking when needed. Use a normal push for a new branch or a fast-forward update. If rebasing rewrote a published branch, use `--force-with-lease=refs/heads/<branch>:<recorded-sha>` against the SHA recorded before the rebase. A rejected lease means someone updated the remote: fetch and reconcile their work before trying again. Never use an unconditional force push.
-
-Call the Skill tool with "pr" to write the PR body from the actual branch diff and observed verification evidence. Use the hosting platform's authenticated CLI or API to open the PR against the selected `main` or `master` base. The pr skill owns the body format; this skill owns publishing it. If an open PR already exists for this head and base, update it rather than creating a duplicate.
-
-Confirm the PR's head, base, and published commit match the intended branch. Return its URL with a concise verification result. Stop at an open PR, not a merge.
-
-**Done when:** the remote contains the intended commits and an open PR targets the selected base, with its URL confirmed by the hosting platform.
~~~~

----
-name: show-me-your-work
-description: Keep an append-only decision trail for long or unattended work.
-disable-model-invocation: true
----
-
-# Show Me Your Work
-
-Keep one **decision trail** while work already authorized by the user is underway. This skill does not start or broaden the underlying task.
-
-1. **Choose the log.** Use the user's named path or an existing log for this effort. Otherwise use a scratch path outside the repo and tell the user where it is. Keep it local by default. Do not commit or publish it unless requested. The coordinating agent is the sole writer; workers return evidence pointers.
-2. **Append decisions as they happen.** Use the bundled helper with one row per consequential choice, pivot, blocker, or verification checkpoint. Cite the evidence rather than pasting output. Use the observed result, including inconclusive or not run. Omit routine actions and redact secrets or private material.
-
-   ```sh
-   bash <skill-dir>/scripts/log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>
-   ```
-
-   Pass each value as one quoted argument. The helper adds a UTC timestamp and keeps each cell on one line. When a fresh session takes over an existing log, read its tail and append a `start` row that identifies the new session and the prior context. Correct a bad row by appending a superseding row, not rewriting history.
-3. **Hand it back.** Spot-check consequential rows against their evidence. Add a correction or a missing decision if needed. Return the path and flag any unverified results or decisions still needing the user. Stop when the reader can trace the important choices without reading the whole transcript.
-
-Adapted from [pstack show-me-your-work](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/b1fbf4b60ac6813b4583ccc356850dafcf492665/pstack/skills/show-me-your-work/SKILL.md). See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

-#!/usr/bin/env bash
-set -euo pipefail
-
-if [[ $# -ne 6 ]]; then
-    printf 'Usage: bash log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>\n' >&2
-    exit 2
-fi
-
-logfile=$1
-shift
-mkdir -p -- "$(dirname -- "$logfile")"
-
-clean() {
-    local cell=$1
-    cell=${cell//$'\t'/ }
-    cell=${cell//$'\n'/ }
-    cell=${cell//$'\r'/ }
-    if [[ $cell =~ ^[[:space:]]*[=+@-] ]]; then
-        cell="'$cell"
-    fi
-    printf '%s' "$cell"
-}
-
-ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
-{
-    if [[ ! -s $logfile ]]; then
-        printf 'ts\tphase\tdecision\twhy\tevidence\tresult\n'
-    fi
-    printf '%s' "$ts"
-    for cell in "$@"; do
-        printf '\t'
-        clean "$cell"
-    done
-    printf '\n'
-} >> "$logfile"

~~~~diff
--- local/skills/statechart/SKILL.md
+++ upstream/(absent)/SKILL.md
@@ -1,87 +0,0 @@
----
-name: statechart
-description: Turn a TLA+ model of a product flow, protocol, or service into a reader-facing Mermaid statechart with counterexample paths. Use when asked to draw state transitions, explain a modeled bug as a path through states, or chart a model from formal-verify.
----
-
-# Statechart
-
-The chart shows how a system moves between states, in the words of the person who reads it. That person, the reader, decides whether the behavior is right.
-
-## Run
-
-Work in a scratch folder outside the repo. For a standalone chart, write a TLA+ spec and its config if the user has not supplied them. If `formal-verify` sent you here, use the exact spec and config it checked, including its bounds and rules, and use the same TLC build where supported. If the chart requires a different checker build, disclose the difference and keep the original verdict authoritative. Put presentation changes in the view, not in the model or config. Then run:
-
-```sh
-<skill dir>/scripts/statechart SPEC.tla [--config FILE] [--view FILE] [--out DIR]
-```
-
-`scripts/statechart.ts` is TypeScript, so run it with a runtime that can execute TypeScript. `scripts/statechart` is a POSIX shell script that picks one. On native Windows, run `node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning <skill dir>/scripts/statechart.ts` with Node 22.18 to 22.x, or Node 23.6 or later.
-
-Use mise to install the pinned TLC and Java on first run (network required), or set `TLA2TOOLS` to the absolute path of an existing `tla2tools.jar` and optionally `JAVA` to a Java 11 or later binary.
-
-## Write the spec
-
-Use these rules when writing a standalone model.
-
-- Write rules that must hold in every state as INVARIANTs. Use a temporal PROPERTY for rules about what eventually happens. A rule can be about a screen, a result, a stored value, or a message. If the model has no variable for a rule, add the variable. Never weaken a rule to make it hold.
-- Write `Next` as a disjunction of the actions, such as `YouPressPlay \/ YouPressStop`. If you do not, TLC names every step `Next`.
-- A state with no step out breaks `NoDeadlock`, also when it is a correct end state. When an INVARIANT or a PROPERTY already has that name, the rule is `CHECK_DEADLOCK`. Add to `Next` an action that is true only in the end states and changes nothing, such as `Done == phase \in {"paid", "failed"} /\ UNCHANGED vars`, and give it a label in `step()`.
-
-## Pick the chart
-
-You do the work that needs judgment: the words on each state and arrow, the phases and their colors, the title, and the report to the reader. Put your work in a view module, and give it with `--view`.
-
-Use only a trusted view module: the compiler executes its JavaScript or TypeScript.
-
-To show the reader's words, the view exports `state(vars)`. The value that `state()` returns picks the form:
-
-- A string gives a flat chart: `export const state = (v) => (v.paid ? "Paid" : "Paying");`
-- An array gives parent states: `export const state = (v) => v.main.split(".");`
-- An object gives one parallel region for each key: `export const state = (v) => ({ Playback: v.playback, Volume: v.volume });`
-
-Label each state with what the reader can see or cares about, such as "Paying" or "Lease held, write pending". Keep variable names out of labels. In `vars`, a TLA+ sequence is an object with keys from 1, so `v.pc[1]` is `pc[1]`. A set is an array.
-
-The view can also export `step(action, from, to)`. It gets the TLC action name and the values before and after the step, and it returns the label of the arrow. Write each step label as the user sees it happen, such as "you press play" or "the connect fails". Do not name the code or the TLA+ action. Two actions that end the same in the chart get the same label, so that they share one arrow.
-
-When a step can occur only in some conditions, end its label with the condition in brackets, in the reader's words, such as `you press play [while the file loads]`. In a regions chart, the command writes the condition on the other regions on the arrow, in the words of their labels, such as `[when Offline]`. Your brackets replace it, and two arrows from one state can then look the same. So in a regions chart, do not write brackets for a condition on another region. When a value that no label shows decides where a step goes, name the result in the label, such as "the roster read fails".
-
-The view can also export these:
-
-- `group(vars)` returns the name of a phase. Each chart state gets the color of its group. When the model states behind one chart state are in different groups, that state gets no color.
-- `colors` gives each group name a color class.
-- `title` is a string that the chart shows at the top.
-
-The command calls `state()` and `group()` at most once for each model state, and `step()` at most once for each step. The chart and the report both use those answers. So make each function depend only on its arguments.
-
-The chart does not draw a step that stays in one label. Split a label when the reader must see such a step.
-
-Aim for about 20 arrows or fewer, because a busier chart is hard to read. First return coarser labels from `state()`. Give one label to values that act the same, and leave out a detail that the reader does not need, such as a call in flight whose return changes nothing. Keep each state of a bug path, and keep each mark. When a merge changes a `breaks` state to `mayBreak`, it hides where a rule breaks. Do not merge two states that break different rules, because the reader then cannot see which rule breaks where. If the chart is still too busy, return `null` from `step()` for the steps that the reader does not need, such as a reset that every state has, or a step whose arrow repeats what other arrows show. Obey these rules when you hide steps:
-
-- Keep each chart state reachable by arrows from a start state.
-- Keep at least one arrow out of each chart state that has a step out in the model.
-- Hide all the steps of an arrow, or none of them. When you hide only some, its condition gets narrower.
-- In the hand-off, say which steps the chart hides.
-
-## Read the report
-
-- In the chart, a state that breaks a rule has the class `breaks`. When only some model states behind it break the rule, it has the class `mayBreak`. The Legend names the rules of each mark. When two rules break, it names both on one mark, so say in the hand-off which state breaks which rule. In a regions chart, a state gets a mark when each combination of region states that includes it can break a rule. When a combination can break a rule and none of its states has a mark, each state in that combination gets a mark.
-- TLC goes past a state that breaks a rule, so the chart shows the states after a bug.
-- Because TLC goes past bugs, a model with no limit on its states can run without end. Keep the constants small, or add a CONSTRAINT.
-- With a VIEW or a SYMMETRY, TLC counts states that it treats as the same as one state, and the chart draws that one state. An arrow can lead to it rather than to the state that the step reaches, and the report says so.
-- TLC checks the rules in each state past a CONSTRAINT or an ACTION_CONSTRAINT, but it does not explore that state or check it for deadlock. When TLC's shortest path for a rule ends in such a state, the chart draws that state, and the report gives that path. The chart does not draw the other states past the bound. A deadlock in such a state does not show. TLC also checks the rules after each step that an ACTION_CONSTRAINT excludes, also when it reaches the next state another way. When TLC's shortest path for a rule ends with such a step, the chart draws that step.
-- The command checks the rules with TLC on the config as written, with one worker. When a rule breaks, the command removes that rule and runs TLC again, until no rule breaks. After the first break, each run stops at 100,000 distinct states, so that a large model does not run without end. When a run reaches that bound or stops on an error, the report lists the rules that it did not check under "Rules not checked", and the chart does not mark them. A rule that is not checked can hold or break. To check it, remove the rules that break from the config, or make the model smaller. The bound adds a module that changes TLC's order of the variables, so for a property TLC can find a different counterexample than a run without the bound.
-- `tlc.out` is what TLC printed on the config as written. When the chart does not show the bug path of a rule that breaks, `tlc-RULE.out` is what TLC printed for the run that found it. When TLC repeats its first warning, plain TLC prints it twice, but `tlc.out` shows it once, because TLC leaves the second copy out of the output that this command reads. That happens only when Java runs with `-XX:+UseParallelGC`, since otherwise TLC's first warning is its advice to pass that flag, which it prints once.
-
-## Show the chart
-
-Show `chart.mmd` to the user as a `mermaid` code block. The chart has a budget of 500 states, counted by TLC on the config as written. Above that, the chart draws only the paths to the rules that break, and when no rule breaks, the command writes no `chart.mmd`. It still checks each rule, and the report gives the state count and each bug path. To see the whole graph, make the model smaller.
-
-When the user asks for an image, or a chart is too large to read as text, follow [the Pele render instructions](references/render.md). Mermaid-only output does not need Pele. Use a different renderer only if the user asks for it.
-
-## Hand off
-
-Give each chart and its Mermaid text to the person who must decide. Add one line for each bug: the rule, the reader's sentence for that rule, and the path as the report numbers it. Say what the model leaves out. Give the command that makes the files again, with a new `--out` folder.
-
-Treat each path as evidence about the model and config, not the implementation. When `formal-verify` sent you here, return the chart and report to that caller for its own evidence hand-off. Otherwise, when the model describes existing code, replay each bug path against the real code, as a test or a live repro, one step for each action. If replay needs the real user-facing surface, call the Skill tool with `verify` for that path. If a bug does not occur, treat it as a model mismatch until you show otherwise. Report model findings and replay results separately, including any paths you could not replay.
-
-
~~~~

-
-## Colors
-
-Pele ignores Mermaid `theme` and `themeVariables`. Set its `--pele-*` CSS variables on `.pele`. https://pele.run/theming lists them. The command gives each state the color class of its group, such as `class sN teal`. It marks each bad state with `class sN breaks` or `class sN mayBreak`, each state on the shortest path to a bug with `class sN bugPath`, and each state that a PROPERTY counterexample repeats forever with `class sN repeats`. Pele puts these classes on the state's node. Color the classes with CSS.
-
-The `.mmd` file has a `classDef` line for `breaks` and for `mayBreak`, so that any Mermaid viewer shows the bug marks. It has no `classDef` for the group colors, `bugPath`, or `repeats`. Pele writes each `classDef` color as a `style` attribute on the node, and a `style` attribute wins over a normal CSS rule. So the rules for the marks below use `!important`. Without it, a dark theme keeps the light mark colors. A bug mark sets the fill and the text, and `bugPath` and `repeats` set the border. Put the mark rules after the group colors, so that a mark shows over the group color.
-
-These colors are suggestions. They are the colors of the old skill. Put them in a `<style>` element at the start of each SVG. Each SVG then follows the light or dark setting of the viewer.

-test("the graph that parseDot returns keeps none of the text it read", () => {
-  v8.setFlagsFromString("--expose-gc");
-  const gc: () => void = vm.runInNewContext("gc");
-  const heapUsed = () => {
-    gc();
-    gc();
-    return process.memoryUsage().heapUsed;
-  };
-  const MiB = 1 << 20;
-  const pieces = 16;
-  function* dot() {
-    for (let i = 0; i < pieces; i++) {
-      const id = `-${String(i).padStart(18, "7")}`;
-      const lines = [
-        `${id} [label="n = ${i}"];`,
-        `${id} -> ${id} [label="StayAtStateNumber${i}"];`,
-      ];
-      while (lines.length < 1024) lines.push(`// ${"x".repeat(1020)}`);
-      yield* `${lines.join("\n")}\n`.split("\n");
-    }
-  }
-  const before = heapUsed();
-  const graph = parseDot(dot());
-  const kept = heapUsed() - before;
-  assert.equal(graph.states.size, pieces);
-  assert.ok(kept < 4 * MiB, `the graph keeps ${(kept / MiB).toFixed(1)} MiB of ${pieces} MiB read`);
-});

-const ab: View = { state: (v) => ({ A: `a${v.a}`, B: `b${v.b}` }) };

-const xorStates: StateRow[] = [];
-const xorSteps: StepRow[] = [];
-for (const a of [0, 1])
-  for (const b of [0, 1])
-    for (const c of [0, 1]) {
-      const v = { a, b, c };
-      xorStates.push([bit(v), v, a === 0]);
-      if (a === 0 && b !== c) xorSteps.push([bit(v), bit({ ...v, a: 1 }), "Go"]);
-      if (b === 0) xorSteps.push([bit(v), bit({ ...v, b: 1 }), "FlipB"]);
-      if (c === 0) xorSteps.push([bit(v), bit({ ...v, c: 1 }), "FlipC"]);
-    }

-  fork: [

-        ["a0b0", "a2b2", "Sync"],

-    ab,

-  partial: [

-        ["a0b0", { a: 0, b: 0 }, true],

-        ["a1b0", { a: 1, b: 0 }],

-function asTlcPrintsOnWindows(text: string) {
-  const lines = text.split("\n");
-  let depth = 0;
-  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length - 1; i++) {
-    if (/@!@!@STARTMSG \d+:\d+ @!@!@$/.test(lines[i])) depth++;
-    else if (/^@!@!@ENDMSG \d+ @!@!@$/.test(lines[i])) depth--;
-    if (!depth) lines[i] += "\r";
-  }
-  return lines.join("\n");
-}

-function startCommand(
-  dir: string,
-  parent: string,
-  {
-    java = path.join(here, "java.ts"),
-    tmpdir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "statechart-tmpdir-")),
-  }: { java?: string; tmpdir?: string } = {},
-) {
-  const name = path.basename(dir);
-  const view = path.join(dir, "view.mjs");
-  return spawn(
-    process.execPath,
-    [
-      path.join(here, "../statechart.ts"),
-      path.join(dir, `${name}.tla`),
-      ...(fs.existsSync(view) ? ["--view", view] : []),
-      "--out",
-      path.join(parent, "out"),
-    ],
-    {
-      env: {
-        ...process.env,
-        JAVA: java,
-        TLA2TOOLS: "tla2tools.jar",
-        STATECHART_REPLAY: dir,
-        TMPDIR: tmpdir,
-      },
-      stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"],
-    },
-  );
-}
-
-async function signalWhile<T extends { dir: string; reached: (parent: string) => boolean }>(
-  signal: NodeJS.Signals,
-  setup: (fakes: string) => T & { java?: string },
-) {
-  const fakes = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "statechart-fakes-"));
-  const parent = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "statechart-parent-"));
-  const tmpdir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "statechart-tmpdir-"));
-  const phase = setup(fakes);
-  const child = startCommand(phase.dir, parent, { java: phase.java, tmpdir });
-  let stderr = "";
-  child.stderr.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => (stderr += chunk));
-  const closed = once(child, "close");
-  const end = Date.now() + 60_000;
-  while (!phase.reached(parent))
-    assert.ok(Date.now() < end, "The command did not reach the phase.");
-  child.kill(signal);
-  const [status] = await closed;
-  assert.equal(stderr, `${signal} stopped the check, so the command wrote nothing.\n`);
-  assert.equal(status, 128 + os.constants.signals[signal]);
-  assert.deepEqual(fs.readdirSync(parent), []);
-  assert.deepEqual(fs.readdirSync(tmpdir), []);
-  return phase;
-}
-
-async function assertGone(pid: number) {
-  for (let i = 0; ; i++) {
-    let code: string | undefined;
-    try {
-      process.kill(pid, 0);
-    } catch (error) {
-      code = (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
-      // macOS gives EPERM for a process group of only zombies, until they are reaped.
-      if (code !== "EPERM") {
-        assert.equal(code, "ESRCH");
-        return;
-      }
-    }
-    assert.ok(
-      i < 250,
-      `Process ${pid} ${code ? "exited, but it was not reaped" : "is still running"}.`,
-    );
-    await sleep(20);
-  }
-}
-
-async function assertEmpty(dir: string) {
-  for (let i = 0; i < 250 && fs.readdirSync(dir).length; i++) await sleep(20);
-  assert.deepEqual(fs.readdirSync(dir), []);
-}

-function gridCase(n: number) {
-  const dir = path.join(fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "statechart-case-")), "Grid");
-  fs.cpSync(path.join(here, "grid"), dir, { recursive: true });
-  for (const run of ["ChartRun.out", "verdict-1.out"])
-    fs.copyFileSync(path.join(corpus, "Login", run), path.join(dir, run));
-  const id = (x: number, y: number) => String(1_000_000 + x * n + y);
-  const lines = ["strict digraph DiskGraph {"];
-  for (let x = 0; x < n; x++)
-    for (let y = 0; y < n; y++) {
-      lines.push(
-        `${id(x, y)} [label="/\\\\ x = ${x}\\n/\\\\ y = ${y}"${x + y ? "" : ",style = filled"}]`,
-      );
-      if (x + 1 < n) lines.push(`${id(x, y)} -> ${id(x + 1, y)} [label="IncX"];`);
-      if (y + 1 < n) lines.push(`${id(x, y)} -> ${id(x, y + 1)} [label="IncY"];`);
-    }
-  lines.push("}");
-  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, "graph.dot"), lines.join("\n"));
-  return dir;
-}

-function sleepyJava(fakes: string) {
-  const java = path.join(fakes, "java.mjs");
-  const pidFile = path.join(fakes, "java.pid");
-  fs.writeFileSync(
-    java,
-    `#!/usr/bin/env node\nimport fs from "node:fs";\n` +
-      `process.on("SIGTERM", () => {});\n` +
-      `fs.writeFileSync(${JSON.stringify(pidFile)}, String(process.pid));\n` +
-      `setTimeout(() => {}, 60_000);\n`,
-    { mode: 0o755 },
-  );
-  return { java, pidFile };
-}

----- MODULE CounterDeadlock ----

-VARIABLE x
-Init == x = 0
-Inc == x < 3 /\ x' = x + 1
-Jump == x = 0 /\ x' = 3
-Next == Inc \/ Jump
-Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_x
-NoJump == ~(x = 0 /\ x' = 3)
-NotThree == x # 3

-# CounterDeadlock
-
-TLC reached 4 states and 3 steps. The chart draws 4 states and 4 arrows.
-1 step that the constraints exclude ends a rule's path, and the chart includes it. TLC checks the rules after such a step, but it does not take the step.
-The chart marks only the deadlock that TLC reports. Under a CONSTRAINT or an ACTION_CONSTRAINT, a state with no step in the chart can still have steps that the constraints leave out, and TLC does not count it as a deadlock.
-
-## NotThree breaks
-The shortest path has 1 step:
-0. 0
-1. Jump: 3
-
-## NoDeadlock breaks
-The shortest path has 3 steps:
-0. 0
-1. Inc: 1
-2. Inc: 2
-3. Inc: 3

@@ -1,15 +0,0 @@
-# CounterOrder
-
-TLC reached 2 states and 1 steps. The chart draws 3 states and 2 arrows.
-1 state outside the constraints ends a rule's path, and the chart includes it. TLC checks the rules in a state outside the constraints, but it does not explore past it.
-The chart marks only the deadlock that TLC reports. Under a CONSTRAINT or an ACTION_CONSTRAINT, a state with no step in the chart can still have steps that the constraints leave out, and TLC does not count it as a deadlock.
-
-## NoDeadlock breaks
-The shortest path has 1 step:
-0. 0
-1. A: 1
-
-## Even breaks
-The shortest path has 1 step:
-0. 0
-1. B: 9

-

----- MODULE CounterTieInGraph ----
-EXTENDS Naturals
-VARIABLE x
-Init == x = 0
-Inc == x < 3 /\ x' = x + 1
-Alpha == x = 0 /\ x' = 3
-Down == x > 0 /\ x' = x - 1
-Next == Inc \/ Alpha \/ Down
-Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_x
-NoDownFromTwo == ~(x = 2 /\ x' = 1)
-OneOrThree == x # 1 /\ x # 3
-====

@@ -1,14 +0,0 @@
----- MODULE CounterView ----
-EXTENDS Naturals
-VARIABLE x
-Init == x = 0
-Inc == x' = x + 1
-Jump == x = 0 /\ x' = 3
-Next == Inc \/ Jump
-Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_x
-Small == x < 5
-NoJump == ~(x = 0 /\ x' = 3)
-NotThree == x # 3
-NotFive == x # 5
-NotOdd == x % 2 = 0
-====

-# CounterView
-
-TLC reached 5 states and 4 steps. The chart draws 4 states and 5 arrows.
-1 state outside the constraints ends a rule's path, and the chart includes it. TLC checks the rules in a state outside the constraints, but it does not explore past it.
-1 step that the constraints exclude ends a rule's path, and the chart includes it. TLC checks the rules after such a step, but it does not take the step.
-
-## NotOdd breaks
-The shortest path has 1 step:
-0. 0
-1. Inc: odd
-
-## NotThree breaks
-The shortest path has 1 step:
-0. 0
-1. Jump: odd
-
-## NotFive breaks
-The shortest path has 5 steps:
-0. 0
-1. Inc: odd
-2. Inc: 2
-3. Inc: odd
-4. Inc: 4
-5. Inc: odd
-
-## Rules that hold
-NoDeadlock
~~~~

@@ -1,38 +0,0 @@
----- MODULE DieHard ----
-\* The classic jug puzzle from Die Hard 3: a 3-gallon jug, a 5-gallon jug,
-\* and a fountain. Get exactly 4 gallons in the big jug.
-EXTENDS Naturals
-
-VARIABLES big, small
-vars == <<big, small>>
-
-Min(m, n) == IF m < n THEN m ELSE n
-
-TypeOK == small \in 0..3 /\ big \in 0..5
-
-Init == big = 0 /\ small = 0
-
-FillSmall == small' = 3 /\ big' = big
-FillBig == big' = 5 /\ small' = small
-EmptySmall == small' = 0 /\ big' = big
-EmptyBig == big' = 0 /\ small' = small
-
-SmallToBig ==
-  /\ big' = Min(big + small, 5)
-  /\ small' = small - (big' - big)
-
-BigToSmall ==
-  /\ small' = Min(big + small, 3)
-  /\ big' = big - (small' - small)
-
-Next ==
-  \/ FillSmall \/ FillBig
-  \/ EmptySmall \/ EmptyBig
-  \/ SmallToBig \/ BigToSmall
-
-Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
-
-\* The puzzle's goal, written as a rule that should break: TLC's
-\* counterexample is the solution.
-NotSolved == big # 4
-====
~~~~

</details>

-# HiddenClock
-
-TLC reached 2 states and 2 steps. The chart draws 2 states and 1 arrows.
-The chart does not draw 1 steps that stay in one chart state.
-With VIEW, TLC keeps one representative for each group of states that it counts as the same. An arrow can lead to the representative rather than to the state that the step reaches.
-
-## EndsAtZero breaks
-TLC's counterexample is in tlc-EndsAtZero.out. It has 1 step:
-0. x=0 clock=0
-1. Tick: x=1 clock=1
-The run stops in "x=1 clock=1" forever.

@@ -1,62 +0,0 @@
----- MODULE Login ----
-\* Generated by chart-to-tla.mjs from login.mmd.
-\* Each region is one variable and each transition label is one action.
-\* Once you add guards and variables from the real code, this file is the source.
-\* statechart.mjs from-chart login.mmd keeps it, checks it, and compares it with the chart.
-
-VARIABLES main
-vars == <<main>>
-
-\* Region Main
-mainStates == {"Locked out", "Reset email sent", "Signed in", "Signed out", "Trying to sign in.Checking first try", "Trying to sign in.Checking last try", "Trying to sign in.Checking second try", "Trying to sign in.Wrong password, 1 try left", "Trying to sign in.Wrong password, 2 tries left"}
-
-TypeOK ==
-    /\ main \in mainStates
-
-Init ==
-    /\ main = "Signed out"
-
-\* the password is right
-ThePasswordIsRight ==
-    /\ \/ (main = "Trying to sign in.Checking first try" /\ main' = "Signed in")
-       \/ (main = "Trying to sign in.Checking second try" /\ main' = "Signed in")
-       \/ (main = "Trying to sign in.Checking last try" /\ main' = "Signed in")
-
-\* the password is wrong
-ThePasswordIsWrong ==
-    /\ \/ (main = "Trying to sign in.Checking first try" /\ main' = "Trying to sign in.Wrong password, 2 tries left")
-       \/ (main = "Trying to sign in.Checking second try" /\ main' = "Trying to sign in.Wrong password, 1 try left")
-       \/ (main = "Trying to sign in.Checking last try" /\ main' = "Locked out")
-
-\* you submit a password
-YouSubmitAPassword ==
-    /\ \/ (main = "Trying to sign in.Wrong password, 2 tries left" /\ main' = "Trying to sign in.Checking second try")
-       \/ (main = "Trying to sign in.Wrong password, 1 try left" /\ main' = "Trying to sign in.Checking last try")
-       \/ (main = "Signed out" /\ main' = "Trying to sign in.Checking first try")
-
-\* you tap Forgot password
-YouTapForgotPassword ==
-    /\ \/ (main = "Trying to sign in.Checking first try" /\ main' = "Reset email sent")
-       \/ (main = "Trying to sign in.Wrong password, 2 tries left" /\ main' = "Reset email sent")
-       \/ (main = "Trying to sign in.Checking second try" /\ main' = "Reset email sent")
-       \/ (main = "Trying to sign in.Wrong password, 1 try left" /\ main' = "Reset email sent")
-       \/ (main = "Trying to sign in.Checking last try" /\ main' = "Reset email sent")
-       \/ (main = "Locked out" /\ main' = "Reset email sent")
-
-\* 15 minutes pass
-S15MinutesPass ==
-    /\ \/ (main = "Locked out" /\ main' = "Signed out")
-
-\* you set a new password
-YouSetANewPassword ==
-    /\ \/ (main = "Reset email sent" /\ main' = "Signed out")
-
-\* you sign out
-YouSignOut ==
-    /\ \/ (main = "Signed in" /\ main' = "Signed out")
-
-Next == ThePasswordIsRight \/ ThePasswordIsWrong \/ YouSubmitAPassword \/ YouTapForgotPassword \/ S15MinutesPass \/ YouSetANewPassword \/ YouSignOut
-
-Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
-
-====

----- MODULE LoginGuarded ----
-\* Generated by chart-to-tla.mjs from login-guarded.mmd.
-\* Each region is one variable and each transition label is one action.
-\* Once you add guards and variables from the real code, this file is the source.
-\* statechart.mjs from-chart login-guarded.mmd keeps it, checks it, and compares it with the chart.
-
-VARIABLES session, wrongTries
-vars == <<session, wrongTries>>
-
-\* Region Session
-sessionStates == {"Checking the password", "Signed in", "Signed out"}
-\* Region Wrong tries
-wrongTriesStates == {"1 wrong try", "2 wrong tries", "Locked out", "No wrong tries"}
-
-TypeOK ==
-    /\ session \in sessionStates
-    /\ wrongTries \in wrongTriesStates
-
-Init ==
-    /\ session = "Signed out"
-    /\ wrongTries = "No wrong tries"
-
-\* you submit a password
-YouSubmitAPassword ==
-    /\ \/ (session = "Signed out" /\ ~(wrongTries = "Locked out") /\ session' = "Checking the password")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<wrongTries>>
-
-\* the password is right
-ThePasswordIsRight ==
-    /\ (session \in {"Checking the password"} \/ (wrongTries = "1 wrong try" /\ session = "Checking the password") \/ (wrongTries = "2 wrong tries" /\ session = "Checking the password"))
-    /\ \/ (session = "Checking the password" /\ session' = "Signed in")
-       \/ (session \notin {"Checking the password"} /\ UNCHANGED session)
-    /\ \/ (wrongTries = "1 wrong try" /\ session = "Checking the password" /\ wrongTries' = "No wrong tries")
-       \/ (wrongTries = "2 wrong tries" /\ session = "Checking the password" /\ wrongTries' = "No wrong tries")
-       \/ (~((wrongTries = "1 wrong try" /\ session = "Checking the password") \/ (wrongTries = "2 wrong tries" /\ session = "Checking the password")) /\ UNCHANGED wrongTries)
-
-\* the password is wrong
-ThePasswordIsWrong ==
-    /\ (session \in {"Checking the password"} \/ (wrongTries = "No wrong tries" /\ session = "Checking the password") \/ (wrongTries = "1 wrong try" /\ session = "Checking the password") \/ (wrongTries = "2 wrong tries" /\ session = "Checking the password"))
-    /\ \/ (session = "Checking the password" /\ session' = "Signed out")
-       \/ (session \notin {"Checking the password"} /\ UNCHANGED session)
-    /\ \/ (wrongTries = "No wrong tries" /\ session = "Checking the password" /\ wrongTries' = "1 wrong try")
-       \/ (wrongTries = "1 wrong try" /\ session = "Checking the password" /\ wrongTries' = "2 wrong tries")
-       \/ (wrongTries = "2 wrong tries" /\ session = "Checking the password" /\ wrongTries' = "Locked out")
-       \/ (~((wrongTries = "No wrong tries" /\ session = "Checking the password") \/ (wrongTries = "1 wrong try" /\ session = "Checking the password") \/ (wrongTries = "2 wrong tries" /\ session = "Checking the password")) /\ UNCHANGED wrongTries)
-
-\* you sign out
-YouSignOut ==
-    /\ \/ (session = "Signed in" /\ session' = "Signed out")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<wrongTries>>
-
-\* 15 minutes pass
-S15MinutesPass ==
-    /\ \/ (wrongTries = "Locked out" /\ wrongTries' = "No wrong tries")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<session>>
-
-Next == YouSubmitAPassword \/ ThePasswordIsRight \/ ThePasswordIsWrong \/ YouSignOut \/ S15MinutesPass
-
-Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
-
-\* A locked-out account never signs in until the lockout ends.
-SignedInWhileLocked == ~(session = "Signed in" /\ wrongTries = "Locked out")
-
-====
~~~~

@@ -1,64 +0,0 @@
----- MODULE LoginParallel ----
-\* Generated by chart-to-tla.mjs from login-parallel.mmd.
-\* Each region is one variable and each transition label is one action.
-\* Once you add guards and variables from the real code, this file is the source.
-\* statechart.mjs from-chart login-parallel.mmd keeps it, checks it, and compares it with the chart.
-
-VARIABLES session, wrongTries
-vars == <<session, wrongTries>>
-
-\* Region Session
-sessionStates == {"Checking the password", "Signed in", "Signed out"}
-\* Region Wrong tries
-wrongTriesStates == {"1 wrong try", "2 wrong tries", "Locked out", "No wrong tries"}
-
-TypeOK ==
-    /\ session \in sessionStates
-    /\ wrongTries \in wrongTriesStates
-
-Init ==
-    /\ session = "Signed out"
-    /\ wrongTries = "No wrong tries"
-
-\* you submit a password
-YouSubmitAPassword ==
-    /\ \/ (session = "Signed out" /\ session' = "Checking the password")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<wrongTries>>
-
-\* the password is right
-ThePasswordIsRight ==
-    /\ (session \in {"Checking the password"} \/ wrongTries \in {"1 wrong try", "2 wrong tries"})
-    /\ \/ (session = "Checking the password" /\ session' = "Signed in")
-       \/ (session \notin {"Checking the password"} /\ UNCHANGED session)
-    /\ \/ (wrongTries = "1 wrong try" /\ wrongTries' = "No wrong tries")
-       \/ (wrongTries = "2 wrong tries" /\ wrongTries' = "No wrong tries")
-       \/ (wrongTries \notin {"1 wrong try", "2 wrong tries"} /\ UNCHANGED wrongTries)
-
-\* the password is wrong
-ThePasswordIsWrong ==
-    /\ (session \in {"Checking the password"} \/ wrongTries \in {"No wrong tries", "1 wrong try", "2 wrong tries"})
-    /\ \/ (session = "Checking the password" /\ session' = "Signed out")
-       \/ (session \notin {"Checking the password"} /\ UNCHANGED session)
-    /\ \/ (wrongTries = "No wrong tries" /\ wrongTries' = "1 wrong try")
-       \/ (wrongTries = "1 wrong try" /\ wrongTries' = "2 wrong tries")
-       \/ (wrongTries = "2 wrong tries" /\ wrongTries' = "Locked out")
-       \/ (wrongTries \notin {"No wrong tries", "1 wrong try", "2 wrong tries"} /\ UNCHANGED wrongTries)
-
-\* you sign out
-YouSignOut ==
-    /\ \/ (session = "Signed in" /\ session' = "Signed out")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<wrongTries>>
-
-\* 15 minutes pass
-S15MinutesPass ==
-    /\ \/ (wrongTries = "Locked out" /\ wrongTries' = "No wrong tries")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<session>>
-
-Next == YouSubmitAPassword \/ ThePasswordIsRight \/ ThePasswordIsWrong \/ YouSignOut \/ S15MinutesPass
-
-Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
-
-\* A locked-out account never signs in until the lockout ends.
-SignedInWhileLocked == ~(session = "Signed in" /\ wrongTries = "Locked out")
-
-====
~~~~

~~~~diff
--- local/skills/statechart/scripts/test/corpus/MediaPlayer/MediaPlayer.tla
+++ upstream/(absent)/scripts/test/corpus/MediaPlayer/MediaPlayer.tla
@@ -1,103 +0,0 @@
----- MODULE MediaPlayer ----
-\* Generated by chart-to-tla.mjs from media-player-fixed.mmd.
-\* Each region is one variable and each transition label is one action.
-\* Once you add guards and variables from the real code, this file is the source.
-\* statechart.mjs from-chart media-player-fixed.mmd keeps it, checks it, and compares it with the chart.
-
-VARIABLES playback, volume
-vars == <<playback, volume>>
-
-\* Region Playback
-playbackStates == {"Buffering", "Paused", "Playing", "Stopped"}
-\* Region Volume
-volumeStates == {"Loud", "Muted", "Normal volume"}
-
-TypeOK ==
-    /\ playback \in playbackStates
-    /\ volume \in volumeStates
-
-Init ==
-    /\ playback = "Stopped"
-    /\ volume = "Normal volume"
-
-\* you press play
-YouPressPlay ==
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Stopped" /\ playback' = "Buffering")
-       \/ (playback = "Paused" /\ playback' = "Playing")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<volume>>
-
-\* enough data arrives
-EnoughDataArrives ==
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Buffering" /\ playback' = "Playing")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<volume>>
-
-\* the network slows
-TheNetworkSlows ==
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Playing" /\ playback' = "Buffering")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<volume>>
-
-\* you press pause
-YouPressPause ==
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Playing" /\ playback' = "Paused")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<volume>>
-
-\* a call comes in
-ACallComesIn ==
-    /\ (playback \in {"Playing"} \/ volume \in {"Normal volume", "Loud"})
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Playing" /\ playback' = "Paused")
-       \/ (playback \notin {"Playing"} /\ UNCHANGED playback)
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Normal volume" /\ volume' = "Muted")
-       \/ (volume = "Loud" /\ volume' = "Muted")
-       \/ (volume \notin {"Normal volume", "Loud"} /\ UNCHANGED volume)
-
-\* the track ends
-TheTrackEnds ==
-    /\ (playback \in {"Playing"} \/ volume \in {"Loud"})
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Playing" /\ playback' = "Stopped")
-       \/ (playback \notin {"Playing"} /\ UNCHANGED playback)
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Loud" /\ volume' = "Normal volume")
-       \/ (volume \notin {"Loud"} /\ UNCHANGED volume)
-
-\* you press stop
-YouPressStop ==
-    /\ (playback \in {"Playing", "Paused", "Buffering"} \/ volume \in {"Loud"})
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Playing" /\ playback' = "Stopped")
-       \/ (playback = "Paused" /\ playback' = "Stopped")
-       \/ (playback = "Buffering" /\ playback' = "Stopped")
-       \/ (playback \notin {"Playing", "Paused", "Buffering"} /\ UNCHANGED playback)
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Loud" /\ volume' = "Normal volume")
-       \/ (volume \notin {"Loud"} /\ UNCHANGED volume)
-
-\* you turn it up
-YouTurnItUp ==
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Normal volume" /\ volume' = "Loud")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<playback>>
-
-\* you turn it down
-YouTurnItDown ==
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Loud" /\ volume' = "Normal volume")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<playback>>
-
-\* you press mute
-YouPressMute ==
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Normal volume" /\ volume' = "Muted")
-       \/ (volume = "Loud" /\ volume' = "Muted")
-       \/ (volume = "Muted" /\ volume' = "Normal volume")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<playback>>
-
-\* the call ends
-TheCallEnds ==
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Muted" /\ volume' = "Normal volume")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<playback>>
-
-Next == YouPressPlay \/ EnoughDataArrives \/ TheNetworkSlows \/ YouPressPause \/ ACallComesIn \/ TheTrackEnds \/ YouPressStop \/ YouTurnItUp \/ YouTurnItDown \/ YouPressMute \/ TheCallEnds
-
-Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
-
-\* The player stops at last.
-EventuallyStops == <>(playback = "Stopped")
-
-\* When nothing plays, the volume is never above the safe level.
-LoudWhenStopped == ~(playback = "Stopped" /\ volume = "Loud")
-
-====
~~~~

-# MediaPlayer
-
-TLC reached 12 states and 64 steps. The chart draws 7 states and 13 arrows.
-The step a call comes in changes Playback and Volume at the same time.
-The step the track ends changes Playback and Volume at the same time.
-The step you press stop changes Playback and Volume at the same time.
-
-## LoudWhenStopped breaks
-The shortest path has 1 step:
-0. Playback Stopped, Volume Normal volume
-1. you turn it up: Playback Stopped, Volume Loud
-
-## Rules that hold
-TypeOK, NoDeadlock, EventuallyStops

~~~~diff
--- local/skills/statechart/scripts/test/corpus/MediaPlayerFixed/MediaPlayerFixed.tla
+++ upstream/(absent)/scripts/test/corpus/MediaPlayerFixed/MediaPlayerFixed.tla
@@ -1,100 +0,0 @@
----- MODULE MediaPlayerFixed ----
-\* Generated by chart-to-tla.mjs from media-player-fixed.mmd.
-\* Each region is one variable and each transition label is one action.
-\* Once you add guards and variables from the real code, this file is the source.
-\* statechart.mjs from-chart media-player-fixed.mmd keeps it, checks it, and compares it with the chart.
-
-VARIABLES playback, volume
-vars == <<playback, volume>>
-
-\* Region Playback
-playbackStates == {"Buffering", "Paused", "Playing", "Stopped"}
-\* Region Volume
-volumeStates == {"Loud", "Muted", "Normal volume"}
-
-TypeOK ==
-    /\ playback \in playbackStates
-    /\ volume \in volumeStates
-
-Init ==
-    /\ playback = "Stopped"
-    /\ volume = "Normal volume"
-
-\* you press play
-YouPressPlay ==
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Stopped" /\ playback' = "Buffering")
-       \/ (playback = "Paused" /\ playback' = "Playing")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<volume>>
-
-\* enough data arrives
-EnoughDataArrives ==
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Buffering" /\ playback' = "Playing")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<volume>>
-
-\* the network slows
-TheNetworkSlows ==
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Playing" /\ playback' = "Buffering")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<volume>>
-
-\* you press pause
-YouPressPause ==
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Playing" /\ playback' = "Paused")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<volume>>
-
-\* a call comes in
-ACallComesIn ==
-    /\ (playback \in {"Playing"} \/ volume \in {"Normal volume", "Loud"})
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Playing" /\ playback' = "Paused")
-       \/ (playback \notin {"Playing"} /\ UNCHANGED playback)
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Normal volume" /\ volume' = "Muted")
-       \/ (volume = "Loud" /\ volume' = "Muted")
-       \/ (volume \notin {"Normal volume", "Loud"} /\ UNCHANGED volume)
-
-\* the track ends
-TheTrackEnds ==
-    /\ (playback \in {"Playing"} \/ volume \in {"Loud"})
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Playing" /\ playback' = "Stopped")
-       \/ (playback \notin {"Playing"} /\ UNCHANGED playback)
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Loud" /\ volume' = "Normal volume")
-       \/ (volume \notin {"Loud"} /\ UNCHANGED volume)
-
-\* you press stop
-YouPressStop ==
-    /\ (playback \in {"Playing", "Paused", "Buffering"} \/ volume \in {"Loud"})
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Playing" /\ playback' = "Stopped")
-       \/ (playback = "Paused" /\ playback' = "Stopped")
-       \/ (playback = "Buffering" /\ playback' = "Stopped")
-       \/ (playback \notin {"Playing", "Paused", "Buffering"} /\ UNCHANGED playback)
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Loud" /\ volume' = "Normal volume")
-       \/ (volume \notin {"Loud"} /\ UNCHANGED volume)
-
-\* you turn it up
-YouTurnItUp ==
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Normal volume" /\ ~(playback = "Stopped") /\ volume' = "Loud")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<playback>>
-
-\* you turn it down
-YouTurnItDown ==
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Loud" /\ volume' = "Normal volume")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<playback>>
-
-\* you press mute
-YouPressMute ==
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Normal volume" /\ volume' = "Muted")
-       \/ (volume = "Loud" /\ volume' = "Muted")
-       \/ (volume = "Muted" /\ volume' = "Normal volume")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<playback>>
-
-\* the call ends
-TheCallEnds ==
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Muted" /\ volume' = "Normal volume")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<playback>>
-
-Next == YouPressPlay \/ EnoughDataArrives \/ TheNetworkSlows \/ YouPressPause \/ ACallComesIn \/ TheTrackEnds \/ YouPressStop \/ YouTurnItUp \/ YouTurnItDown \/ YouPressMute \/ TheCallEnds
-
-Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
-
-\* When nothing plays, the volume is never above the safe level.
-LoudWhenStopped == ~(playback = "Stopped" /\ volume = "Loud")
-
-====
~~~~

@@ -1,103 +0,0 @@
----- MODULE MediaPlayer ----
-\* Generated by chart-to-tla.mjs from media-player-fixed.mmd.
-\* Each region is one variable and each transition label is one action.
-\* Once you add guards and variables from the real code, this file is the source.
-\* statechart.mjs from-chart media-player-fixed.mmd keeps it, checks it, and compares it with the chart.
-
-VARIABLES playback, volume
-vars == <<playback, volume>>
-
-\* Region Playback
-playbackStates == {"Buffering", "Paused", "Playing", "Stopped"}
-\* Region Volume
-volumeStates == {"Loud", "Muted", "Normal volume"}
-
-TypeOK ==
-    /\ playback \in playbackStates
-    /\ volume \in volumeStates
-
-Init ==
-    /\ playback = "Stopped"
-    /\ volume = "Normal volume"
-
-\* you press play
-YouPressPlay ==
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Stopped" /\ playback' = "Buffering")
-       \/ (playback = "Paused" /\ playback' = "Playing")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<volume>>
-
-\* enough data arrives
-EnoughDataArrives ==
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Buffering" /\ playback' = "Playing")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<volume>>
-
-\* the network slows
-TheNetworkSlows ==
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Playing" /\ playback' = "Buffering")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<volume>>
-
-\* you press pause
-YouPressPause ==
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Playing" /\ playback' = "Paused")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<volume>>
-
-\* a call comes in
-ACallComesIn ==
-    /\ (playback \in {"Playing"} \/ volume \in {"Normal volume", "Loud"})
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Playing" /\ playback' = "Paused")
-       \/ (playback \notin {"Playing"} /\ UNCHANGED playback)
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Normal volume" /\ volume' = "Muted")
-       \/ (volume = "Loud" /\ volume' = "Muted")
-       \/ (volume \notin {"Normal volume", "Loud"} /\ UNCHANGED volume)
-
-\* the track ends
-TheTrackEnds ==
-    /\ (playback \in {"Playing"} \/ volume \in {"Loud"})
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Playing" /\ playback' = "Stopped")
-       \/ (playback \notin {"Playing"} /\ UNCHANGED playback)
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Loud" /\ volume' = "Normal volume")
-       \/ (volume \notin {"Loud"} /\ UNCHANGED volume)
-
-\* you press stop
-YouPressStop ==
-    /\ (playback \in {"Playing", "Paused", "Buffering"} \/ volume \in {"Loud"})
-    /\ \/ (playback = "Playing" /\ playback' = "Stopped")
-       \/ (playback = "Paused" /\ playback' = "Stopped")
-       \/ (playback = "Buffering" /\ playback' = "Stopped")
-       \/ (playback \notin {"Playing", "Paused", "Buffering"} /\ UNCHANGED playback)
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Loud" /\ volume' = "Normal volume")
-       \/ (volume \notin {"Loud"} /\ UNCHANGED volume)
-
-\* you turn it up
-YouTurnItUp ==
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Normal volume" /\ volume' = "Loud")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<playback>>
-
-\* you turn it down
-YouTurnItDown ==
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Loud" /\ volume' = "Normal volume")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<playback>>
-
-\* you press mute
-YouPressMute ==
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Normal volume" /\ volume' = "Muted")
-       \/ (volume = "Loud" /\ volume' = "Muted")
-       \/ (volume = "Muted" /\ volume' = "Normal volume")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<playback>>
-
-\* the call ends
-TheCallEnds ==
-    /\ \/ (volume = "Muted" /\ volume' = "Normal volume")
-    /\ UNCHANGED <<playback>>
-
-Next == YouPressPlay \/ EnoughDataArrives \/ TheNetworkSlows \/ YouPressPause \/ ACallComesIn \/ TheTrackEnds \/ YouPressStop \/ YouTurnItUp \/ YouTurnItDown \/ YouPressMute \/ TheCallEnds
-
-Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
-
-\* The player stops at last.
-EventuallyStops == <>(playback = "Stopped")
-
-\* When nothing plays, the volume is never above the safe level.
-LoudWhenStopped == ~(playback = "Stopped" /\ volume = "Loud")
-
-====

-# MediaPlayerProps
-
-TLC reached 12 states and 64 steps. The chart draws 7 states and 13 arrows.
-The step a call comes in changes Playback and Volume at the same time.
-The step the track ends changes Playback and Volume at the same time.
-The step you press stop changes Playback and Volume at the same time.
-
-## EventuallyPlays breaks
-TLC's counterexample is in tlc-EventuallyPlays.out. It has 0 steps:
-0. Playback Stopped, Volume Normal volume
-The run stops in "Playback Stopped, Volume Normal volume" forever.
-
-## QuietWhenStopped breaks
-TLC's counterexample is in tlc-QuietWhenStopped.out. It has 1 step:
-0. Playback Stopped, Volume Normal volume
-1. you turn it up: Playback Stopped, Volume Loud
-
-## Rules that hold
-TypeOK, NoDeadlock, EventuallyStops, StaysTyped

~~~~diff
--- local/skills/statechart/scripts/test/corpus/TwoPhase/TwoPhase.tla
+++ upstream/(absent)/scripts/test/corpus/TwoPhase/TwoPhase.tla
@@ -1,75 +0,0 @@
----- MODULE TwoPhase ----
-\* Lamport's two-phase commit, with one seeded bug: the transaction manager
-\* commits as soon as any resource manager has prepared, not all of them.
-CONSTANT RM
-
-VARIABLES rmState, tmState, tmPrepared, msgs
-vars == <<rmState, tmState, tmPrepared, msgs>>
-
-Messages == [type : {"Prepared"}, rm : RM] \cup [type : {"Commit", "Abort"}]
-
-TPTypeOK ==
-  /\ rmState \in [RM -> {"working", "prepared", "committed", "aborted"}]
-  /\ tmState \in {"init", "done"}
-  /\ tmPrepared \subseteq RM
-  /\ msgs \subseteq Messages
-
-TPInit ==
-  /\ rmState = [r \in RM |-> "working"]
-  /\ tmState = "init"
-  /\ tmPrepared = {}
-  /\ msgs = {}
-
-TMRcvPrepared(r) ==
-  /\ tmState = "init"
-  /\ [type |-> "Prepared", rm |-> r] \in msgs
-  /\ tmPrepared' = tmPrepared \cup {r}
-  /\ UNCHANGED <<rmState, tmState, msgs>>
-
-TMCommit ==
-  /\ tmState = "init"
-  /\ tmPrepared # {}
-  /\ tmState' = "done"
-  /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[type |-> "Commit"]}
-  /\ UNCHANGED <<rmState, tmPrepared>>
-
-TMAbort ==
-  /\ tmState = "init"
-  /\ tmState' = "done"
-  /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[type |-> "Abort"]}
-  /\ UNCHANGED <<rmState, tmPrepared>>
-
-RMPrepare(r) ==
-  /\ rmState[r] = "working"
-  /\ rmState' = [rmState EXCEPT ![r] = "prepared"]
-  /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[type |-> "Prepared", rm |-> r]}
-  /\ UNCHANGED <<tmState, tmPrepared>>
-
-RMChooseToAbort(r) ==
-  /\ rmState[r] = "working"
-  /\ rmState' = [rmState EXCEPT ![r] = "aborted"]
-  /\ UNCHANGED <<tmState, tmPrepared, msgs>>
-
-RMRcvCommitMsg(r) ==
-  /\ [type |-> "Commit"] \in msgs
-  /\ rmState' = [rmState EXCEPT ![r] = "committed"]
-  /\ UNCHANGED <<tmState, tmPrepared, msgs>>
-
-RMRcvAbortMsg(r) ==
-  /\ [type |-> "Abort"] \in msgs
-  /\ rmState' = [rmState EXCEPT ![r] = "aborted"]
-  /\ UNCHANGED <<tmState, tmPrepared, msgs>>
-
-TPNext ==
-  \/ TMCommit \/ TMAbort
-  \/ \E r \in RM :
-       TMRcvPrepared(r) \/ RMPrepare(r) \/ RMChooseToAbort(r)
-         \/ RMRcvCommitMsg(r) \/ RMRcvAbortMsg(r)
-
-TPSpec == TPInit /\ [][TPNext]_vars
-
-\* No resource manager commits while another aborts.
-TCConsistent ==
-  \A r1, r2 \in RM : ~ /\ rmState[r1] = "aborted"
-                       /\ rmState[r2] = "committed"
-====
~~~~

</details>

--- local/skills/statechart/scripts/test/corpus/TwoPhaseFixed/TwoPhaseFixed.tla
+++ upstream/(absent)/scripts/test/corpus/TwoPhaseFixed/TwoPhaseFixed.tla
@@ -1,75 +0,0 @@
----- MODULE TwoPhaseFixed ----
-\* Lamport's two-phase commit: the transaction manager commits only when every
-\* resource manager has prepared.
-CONSTANT RM
-
-VARIABLES rmState, tmState, tmPrepared, msgs
-vars == <<rmState, tmState, tmPrepared, msgs>>
-
-Messages == [type : {"Prepared"}, rm : RM] \cup [type : {"Commit", "Abort"}]
-
-TPTypeOK ==
-  /\ rmState \in [RM -> {"working", "prepared", "committed", "aborted"}]
-  /\ tmState \in {"init", "done"}
-  /\ tmPrepared \subseteq RM
-  /\ msgs \subseteq Messages
-
-TPInit ==
-  /\ rmState = [r \in RM |-> "working"]
-  /\ tmState = "init"
-  /\ tmPrepared = {}
-  /\ msgs = {}
-
-TMRcvPrepared(r) ==
-  /\ tmState = "init"
-  /\ [type |-> "Prepared", rm |-> r] \in msgs
-  /\ tmPrepared' = tmPrepared \cup {r}
-  /\ UNCHANGED <<rmState, tmState, msgs>>
-
-TMCommit ==
-  /\ tmState = "init"
-  /\ tmPrepared = RM
-  /\ tmState' = "done"
-  /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[type |-> "Commit"]}
-  /\ UNCHANGED <<rmState, tmPrepared>>
-
-TMAbort ==
-  /\ tmState = "init"
-  /\ tmState' = "done"
-  /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[type |-> "Abort"]}
-  /\ UNCHANGED <<rmState, tmPrepared>>
-
-RMPrepare(r) ==
-  /\ rmState[r] = "working"
-  /\ rmState' = [rmState EXCEPT ![r] = "prepared"]
-  /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[type |-> "Prepared", rm |-> r]}
-  /\ UNCHANGED <<tmState, tmPrepared>>
-
-RMChooseToAbort(r) ==
-  /\ rmState[r] = "working"
-  /\ rmState' = [rmState EXCEPT ![r] = "aborted"]
-  /\ UNCHANGED <<tmState, tmPrepared, msgs>>
-
-RMRcvCommitMsg(r) ==
-  /\ [type |-> "Commit"] \in msgs
-  /\ rmState' = [rmState EXCEPT ![r] = "committed"]
-  /\ UNCHANGED <<tmState, tmPrepared, msgs>>
-
-RMRcvAbortMsg(r) ==
-  /\ [type |-> "Abort"] \in msgs
-  /\ rmState' = [rmState EXCEPT ![r] = "aborted"]
-  /\ UNCHANGED <<tmState, tmPrepared, msgs>>
-
-TPNext ==
-  \/ TMCommit \/ TMAbort
-  \/ \E r \in RM :
-       TMRcvPrepared(r) \/ RMPrepare(r) \/ RMChooseToAbort(r)
-         \/ RMRcvCommitMsg(r) \/ RMRcvAbortMsg(r)
-
-TPSpec == TPInit /\ [][TPNext]_vars
-
-\* No resource manager commits while another aborts.
-TCConsistent ==
-  \A r1, r2 \in RM : ~ /\ rmState[r1] = "aborted"
-                       /\ rmState[r2] = "committed"
-====
~~~~

</details>

-const GROUPS = ["paying", "a b", ...PROTOTYPE_KEYS];
-const COLORS = ["blue", "orange", "purple", "yellow"];

-const INT = fc.integer({ min: -3, max: 3 }).map(String);
-const STRING = fc.constantFrom(
-  String.raw`""`,
-  String.raw`"a b"`,
-  String.raw`"say \"hi\""`,
-  String.raw`"back\\slash"`,
-  String.raw`"tab\tstop"`,
-  String.raw`"two\nlines"`,
-  String.raw`"__proto__"`,
-);
-const values = (value: fc.Arbitrary<string>, maxLength = 4) =>
-  fc.uniqueArray(value, { minLength: 1, maxLength });
-const tuple = (items: string[]) => `<<${items.join(", ")}>>`;
-
-type Domain = string[] | { modelValues: number };
-const DOMAIN: fc.Arbitrary<Domain> = fc.oneof(
-  values(INT),
-  values(STRING),
-  values(fc.constantFrom("TRUE", "FALSE"), 2),
-  fc.integer({ min: 1, max: 4 }).map((modelValues) => ({ modelValues })),
-  values(fc.tuple(INT, STRING).map(([i, s]) => `[constructor |-> ${i}, __proto__ |-> ${s}]`)),
-  values(
-    fc
-      .uniqueArray(fc.tuple(INT, STRING), { maxLength: 2 })
-      .map((ps) => `{${ps.map(tuple).join(", ")}}`),
-  ),
-  values(fc.array(INT, { maxLength: 2 }).map(tuple)),
-);
-
-const ATOM = fc.record({ v: fc.nat(2), i: fc.nat(3), not: fc.boolean() });
-type Atom = { v: number; i: number; not: boolean };
-
-const MODEL = fc.record({
-  module: fc.constantFrom("Model", "prototype"),
-  names: fc.shuffledSubarray(NAMES, { minLength: NAMES.length }),
-  vars: fc.array(
-    fc.record({ domain: DOMAIN, init: fc.array(fc.nat(3), { minLength: 1, maxLength: 2 }) }),
-    { minLength: 1, maxLength: 3 },
-  ),
-  actions: fc.array(
-    fc.record({
-      guard: fc.array(ATOM, { maxLength: 2 }),
-      set: fc.array(
-        fc.record({ v: fc.nat(2), to: fc.array(fc.nat(3), { minLength: 1, maxLength: 2 }) }),
-        { minLength: 1, maxLength: 2 },
-      ),
-    }),
-    { minLength: 1, maxLength: 6 },
-  ),
-  invariants: fc.array(fc.array(ATOM, { minLength: 1, maxLength: 2 }), { maxLength: 2 }),
-  deadlock: fc.boolean(),
-  initNext: fc.boolean(),
-  constraint: fc.option(ATOM, { freq: 2 }),
-  actionConstraint: fc.option(fc.record({ v: fc.nat(2), from: fc.nat(3), to: fc.nat(3) }), {
-    freq: 2,
-  }),
-  property: fc.option(
-    fc.record({
-      form: fc.nat(3),
-      atoms: fc.tuple(ATOM, ATOM),
-      fairness: fc.option(fc.record({ strong: fc.boolean(), on: fc.option(fc.nat(5)) })),
-    }),
-  ),
-  view: fc.option(
-    fc.record({
-      form: fc.constantFrom("string", "parents", "regions"),
-      labels: fc.uniqueArray(fc.constantFrom(...LABELS), { minLength: 1, maxLength: 4 }),
-      regions: fc.uniqueArray(fc.constantFrom("Session", ...LABELS), {
-        minLength: 1,
-        maxLength: 3,
-      }),
-      steps: fc.option(fc.array(fc.option(fc.constantFrom(...STEPS)), { maxLength: 6 })),
-      title: fc.option(fc.constantFrom("A b c", "constructor")),
-      groups: fc.option(fc.uniqueArray(fc.constantFrom(...GROUPS), { minLength: 1, maxLength: 3 })),
-    }),
-  ),
-});
-type Model = typeof MODEL extends fc.Arbitrary<infer M> ? M : never;
-type Case = {
-  module: string;
-  tla: string;
-  view?: string;
-  base: string[];
-  invariants: string[];
-  deadlock: boolean;
-  property?: string;
-};
-
-const configOf = (c: Case) => {
-  const cfg = [...c.base];
-  if (c.invariants.length) cfg.push(`INVARIANTS ${c.invariants.join(" ")}`);
-  if (!c.deadlock) cfg.push("CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE");
-  if (c.property) cfg.push(`PROPERTY ${c.property}`);
-  return `${cfg.join("\n")}\n`;
-};
-
-function caseOf(m: Model): Case {
-  let next = 0;
-  const name = () => m.names[next++];
-  const vars = m.vars.map(name);
-  const domains = m.vars.map(({ domain }) =>
-    Array.isArray(domain) ? domain : Array.from({ length: domain.modelValues }, name),
-  );
-  const modelValues = m.vars.flatMap(({ domain }, k) => (Array.isArray(domain) ? [] : domains[k]));
-  const value = (v: number, i: number) =>
-    domains[v % vars.length][i % domains[v % vars.length].length];
-  const atom = ({ v, i, not }: Atom) =>
-    `${vars[v % vars.length]} ${not ? "#" : "="} ${value(v, i)}`;
-  const set = (v: number, is: number[]) =>
-    `{${[...new Set(is.map((i) => value(v, i)))].join(", ")}}`;
-  const defs = [`vars == <<${vars.join(", ")}>>`];
-  defs.push(`Init == ${vars.map((x, k) => `${x} \\in ${set(k, m.vars[k].init)}`).join(" /\\ ")}`);
-  const actions = m.actions.map((a) => {
-    const changed = new Map<number, number[]>();
-    for (const s of a.set)
-      if (!changed.has(s.v % vars.length)) changed.set(s.v % vars.length, s.to);
-    const parts = a.guard.map(atom);
-    for (const [k, to] of changed) parts.push(`${vars[k]}' \\in ${set(k, to)}`);
-    const kept = vars.filter((_, k) => !changed.has(k));
-    if (kept.length) parts.push(`UNCHANGED <<${kept.join(", ")}>>`);
-    const action = name();
-    defs.push(`${action} == ${parts.join(" /\\ ")}`);
-    return action;
-  });
-  defs.push(`Next == ${actions.join(" \\/ ")}`);
-  const base = modelValues.length
-    ? [`CONSTANTS ${modelValues.map((c) => `${c} = ${c}`).join(" ")}`]
-    : [];
-  const p = m.property;
-  const f = p?.fairness;
-  const fair = f
-    ? ` /\\ ${f.strong ? "SF" : "WF"}_vars(${f.on === null ? "Next" : actions[f.on % actions.length]})`
-    : "";
-  defs.push(`Spec == Init /\\ [][Next]_vars${fair}`);
-  base.push(m.initNext && !p ? "INIT Init\nNEXT Next" : "SPECIFICATION Spec");
-  const invariants = m.invariants.map((atoms) => {
-    const rule = name();
-    defs.push(`${rule} == ~(${atoms.map(atom).join(" /\\ ")})`);
-    return rule;
-  });
-  if (m.constraint) {
-    const bound = name();
-    defs.push(`${bound} == ~(${atom(m.constraint)})`);
-    base.push(`CONSTRAINT ${bound}`);
-  }
-  if (m.actionConstraint) {
-    const { v, from, to } = m.actionConstraint;
-    const x = vars[v % vars.length];
-    const bound = name();
-    defs.push(`${bound} == ~(${x} = ${value(v, from)} /\\ ${x}' = ${value(v, to)})`);
-    base.push(`ACTION_CONSTRAINT ${bound}`);
-  }
-  let property: string | undefined;
-  if (p) {
-    const [a, b] = p.atoms.map(atom);
-    property = name();
-    defs.push(
-      `${property} == ${[`<>(${a})`, `[]<>(${a})`, `(${a}) ~> (${b})`, `[](${a})`][p.form]}`,
-    );
-  }
-  const tla = [
-    `---- MODULE ${m.module} ----`,
-    "EXTENDS Integers",
-    ...(modelValues.length ? [`CONSTANTS ${modelValues.join(", ")}`] : []),
-    `VARIABLES ${vars.join(", ")}`,
-    ...defs,
-    "====",
-    "",
-  ].join("\n");
-  return {
-    module: m.module,
-    tla,
-    view: m.view ? viewOf(m.view, vars, actions) : undefined,
-    base,
-    invariants,
-    deadlock: m.deadlock,
-    property,
-  };
-}
-
-function viewOf(v: NonNullable<Model["view"]>, vars: string[], actions: string[]) {
-  const json = JSON.stringify;
-  const state = {
-    string: `pick(VARS.map((n) => v[n]), 0)`,
-    parents: `[pick(v[VARS[0]], 1), pick(VARS.map((n) => v[n]), 2)]`,
-    regions: `Object.fromEntries(${json(v.regions)}.map((r, k) => [r, pick(v[VARS[k % VARS.length]], k)]))`,
-  }[v.form];
-  const lines = [
-    `const VARS = ${json(vars)};`,
-    `const LABELS = ${json(v.labels)};`,
-    "const pick = (value, salt, from = LABELS) => {",
-    "  let h = salt;",
-    '  for (const c of JSON.stringify(value) ?? "") h = (h * 31 + c.codePointAt(0)) >>> 0;',
-    "  return from[h % from.length];",
-    "};",
-    `export const state = (v) => ${state};`,
-  ];
-  const { steps } = v;
-  if (steps) {
-    const labels = actions.map((a, k) => [a, k < steps.length ? steps[k] : a]);
-    lines.push(
-      `const STEPS = new Map(${json(labels)});`,
-      "export const step = (action) => STEPS.get(action);",
-    );
-  }
-  if (v.title) lines.push(`export const title = ${json(v.title)};`);
-  if (v.groups) {
-    const colors = v.groups.map((g, k) => [g, COLORS[k]]);
-    lines.push(
-      `export const colors = Object.fromEntries(${json(colors)});`,
-      `export const group = (v) => pick(v[VARS[0]], 3, ${json(v.groups)});`,
-    );
-  }
-  return `${lines.join("\n")}\n`;
-}
-
-type Run = { status: number | null; stdout: string; stderr: string };
-
-const run = (command: string, args: string[], cwd: string) =>
-  new Promise<Run>((resolve, reject) => {
-    const child = spawn(command, args, {
-      cwd,
-      stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"],
-      env: { ...process.env, LC_ALL: "C.UTF-8" },
-    });
-    const stdout: Buffer[] = [];
-    const stderr: Buffer[] = [];
-    child.stdout.on("data", (b: Buffer) => stdout.push(b));
-    child.stderr.on("data", (b: Buffer) => stderr.push(b));
-    child.on("error", reject);
-    child.on("close", (status) =>
-      resolve({
-        status,
-        stdout: Buffer.concat(stdout).toString(),
-        stderr: Buffer.concat(stderr).toString(),
-      }),
-    );
-  });
-
-const plainTlc = (dir: string, c: Case, name: string, lines: string[]) => {
-  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, `${name}.cfg`), `${[...c.base, ...lines].join("\n")}\n`);
-  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(dir, `tmp-${name}`));
-  return run(
-    process.env.JAVA || "java",
-    [
-      `-Djava.io.tmpdir=${path.join(dir, `tmp-${name}`)}`,
-      "-cp",
-      String(process.env.TLA2TOOLS),
-      "tlc2.TLC",
-      "-tool",
-      "-workers",
-      "1",
-      "-config",
-      `${name}.cfg`,
-      "-metadir",
-      path.join(dir, `meta-${name}`),
-      c.module,
-    ],
-    dir,
-  );
-};
-
-type Claim = { breaks: boolean; steps?: number };
-
-const claimOf = (r: Run, breaks: number[], traced: boolean): Claim => {
-  if (r.status === 0) return { breaks: false };
-  if (r.status === null || !breaks.includes(r.status))
-    throw new Error(`plain TLC exited ${r.status}:\n${r.stdout}${r.stderr}`);
-  if (!traced) return { breaks: true };
-  const states = r.stdout.split("@!@!@STARTMSG 2217:").length - 1;
-  return { breaks: true, steps: Math.max(states, 1) - 1 };
-};
-
-async function plainAnswers(dir: string, c: Case) {
-  const rules = new Map<string, Promise<Claim>>();
-  for (const name of c.invariants)
-    rules.set(
-      name,
-      plainTlc(dir, c, `inv-${name}`, [`INVARIANT ${name}`, "CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE"]).then((r) =>
-        claimOf(r, [12], true),
-      ),
-    );
-  if (c.deadlock)
-    rules.set(
-      "NoDeadlock",
-      plainTlc(dir, c, "deadlock", []).then((r) => claimOf(r, [11], true)),
-    );
-  if (c.property)
-    rules.set(
-      c.property,
-      plainTlc(dir, c, "property", [`PROPERTY ${c.property}`, "CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE"]).then((r) =>
-        claimOf(r, [12, 13], false),
-      ),
-    );
-  const states = plainTlc(dir, c, "states", ["CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE"]).then((r) => {
-    const found = /([\d,]+) distinct states found/.exec(r.stdout);
-    if (r.status !== 0 || !found)
-      throw new Error(`plain TLC exited ${r.status}:\n${r.stdout}${r.stderr}`);
-    return Number(found[1].replaceAll(",", ""));
-  });
-  const answers = new Map<string, Claim>();
-  for (const [name, claim] of rules) answers.set(name, await claim);
-  const broke = [...answers.values()].some((a) => a.breaks);
-  return { status: broke ? 1 : 0, states: await states, rules: answers };
-}
-
-function compilerAnswers(r: Run, c: Case) {
-  const lines = r.stdout.split("\n");
-  const rules = new Map<string, Claim>();
-  for (const [i, line] of lines.entries()) {
-    const broken = /^## (\S+) breaks$/.exec(line);
-    if (broken) {
-      const shortest = /^The shortest path has (\d+) steps?:$/.exec(lines[i + 1]);
-      rules.set(
-        broken[1],
-        broken[1] === c.property
-          ? { breaks: true }
-          : { breaks: true, steps: Number(shortest?.[1]) },
-      );
-    }
-    if (line === "## Rules that hold")
-      for (const name of lines[i + 1].split(", ")) rules.set(name, { breaks: false });
-  }
-  const states = /^TLC reached (\d+) states/m.exec(r.stdout);
-  return { status: r.status, states: states ? Number(states[1]) : r.stderr, rules };
-}
-
-async function answer(c: Case) {
-  const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "statechart-differential-"));
-  try {
-    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, `${c.module}.tla`), c.tla);
-    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, `${c.module}.cfg`), configOf(c));
-    if (c.view !== undefined) fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, "view.mjs"), c.view);
-    const compile = (view: string[]) =>
-      run(
-        process.execPath,
-        [path.join(here, "../statechart.ts"), `${c.module}.tla`, ...view, "--out", "out"],
-        dir,
-      );
-    const [viewed, plain] = await Promise.all([
-      compile(c.view === undefined ? [] : ["--view", "view.mjs"]),
-      plainAnswers(dir, c),
-    ]);
-    const refused =
-      c.view !== undefined &&
-      viewed.status === 2 &&
-      /^(The view's |The chart draws the step )/.test(viewed.stderr);
-    const compiled = refused ? await compile([]) : viewed;
-    assert.deepEqual(compilerAnswers(compiled, c), plain);
-    return compiled.stdout;
-  } finally {
-    fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
-  }
-}

-const random = (seed: number) => {
-  let a = seed >>> 0;

-    a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) >>> 0;

-    return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;

-  return {
-    int,
-    range: (lo: number, hi: number) => lo + int(hi - lo + 1),
-    chance: (p: number) => next() < p,
-    pick: <T>(items: readonly T[]) => items[int(items.length)],
-  };
-};

-type Random = ReturnType<typeof random>;

-const label = (r: Random) => {

-    const k = r.int(13);
-    if (k < 4) s += r.pick(WORDS);
-    else if (k < 7) s += r.pick(SYNTAX);
-    else if (k < 9) s += r.pick(SPACE);
-    else if (k < 11) s += r.pick(OTHER);
-    else s += String.fromCharCode(32 + r.int(95));
-  }
-  return s;
-};

-  const k = r.int(3);
-  if (k === 0) return r.pick(BAD_COLORS);
-  if (k === 1) return r.pick(THEME) + r.pick(SPACE) + label(r);
-  return label(r);

-const several = <T>(n: number, make: () => T) => {
-  const out: T[] = [];
-  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) out.push(make());

-type Shape =

-type Groups =
-  | { groups?: undefined; colors?: undefined; groupOf?: undefined }
-  | { groups: number[]; colors: unknown[]; groupOf: number[] };

-type Case = Shape &

-function generate(r: Random): Case {
-  const labels: string[] = [];
-  const slot = () => labels.push(label(r)) - 1;
-  const k = r.int(10);
-  const mode = k < 4 ? "flat" : k < 7 ? "parents" : "regions";
-  const n = r.range(2, 4);
-  let shape: Shape;
-  if (mode === "regions") {
-    shape = {
-      mode,
-      regions: [slot(), slot()],
-      pools: [
-        [slot(), slot()],
-        [slot(), slot()],
-      ],
-      values: several(n, () => [r.int(2), r.int(2)]),
-    };
-  } else {
-    const leaf = several(n, slot);
-    if (mode === "parents") {
-      const parents = r.chance(0.5) ? [slot(), slot()] : [slot()];
-      const parentOf = several(n, () => (r.chance(0.75) ? r.int(parents.length) : -1));
-      shape = { mode, leaf, parents, parentOf };
-    } else shape = { mode, leaf };
-  }
-  const actions = several(r.range(1, 3), slot);
-  const steps = several(r.range(1, 5), () => [r.int(n), r.int(n), r.int(actions.length)]);
-  let groups: Groups = {};
-  if (r.chance(0.4)) {
-    const named = several(r.range(1, 2), slot);
-    const colors = several(named.length, () => color(r));
-    const groupOf = several(n, () => (r.chance(0.8) ? r.int(named.length) : -1));
-    groups = { groups: named, colors, groupOf };
-  }
-  const title = r.chance(0.3) ? slot() : undefined;
-  return { ...shape, ...groups, n, labels, actions, steps, title };
-}
